# Somo curriculum (generated)

*Generated by `tools/gen-curriculum.mjs` from the skill graph in the code. Do not edit by hand: change the code and run the tool again.*

Somo teaches Grade 1 foundational literacy and numeracy. Every skill has a stage (1 Mbegu, 2 Chipukizi, 3 Mti, 4 Matunda), a strand, prerequisites and three teaching steps (Watch → Together → You). Skills marked **path** are units on the learning path (Inspire → Interpret → Impart). Skills marked **games** are practised in the games library (Michezo) and open when their prerequisites are met.

## Mastery

Each skill moves through five states: not introduced, learning, practising, independent, mastered. **Mastered** needs 4 of the last 5 answers right with no help, on at least 2 different days, the newest on a later day (a spaced review). Answers after a hint or a miss count as practising, never mastery. A skill that slips drops back by itself. Stars: practising 1, independent 2, mastered 3.

## The plug-in games

| Game | Kiswahili | Skills | Stages | Ages | Levels | What the child does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sauti Sokoni (`sauti-sokoni`) | Sauti Sokoni | First, last and middle sounds | 1, 2 | 5–7 | 3 | The market seller calls a sound. Put the things with that sound in the kiondo basket. Level 1: first sound; level 2: last sound; level 3: middle sound. |
| Ngoma Beats (`ngoma-beats`) | Mdundo wa Ngoma | Syllables (beats in words) | 1, 2 | 5–7 | 3 | Hear a word and tap the drum once for each beat (ma-ta-tu is 3). Level 2: find the picture with that many beats. Level 3: join two word parts into one word. |
| Sound Boxes (`sound-boxes`) | Visanduku vya Sauti | Segmenting (pulling a word into its sounds) | 2 | 5–8 | 3 | Hear a word and put a bead in a box for each sound. Level 2: use letter tiles instead of beads. Level 3: four-sound words like frog and nest. |
| Matatu Spell (`matatu-spell`) | Tahajia ya Matatu | Blending and spelling short words | 2, 3 | 6–8 | 3 | The route sign shows a picture. Board the letter passengers in order to spell it; the conductor blends the sounds as each one boards. Only letters the child has learned. |
| Real or Silly? (`real-or-silly`) | Kweli au Kichekesho? | Reading made-up words (true decoding) | 3 | 6–9 | 3 | Mangoes carry words. Read each one and put it in the real-word basket or the silly-word basket. Made-up words like zim test true sounding-out. |
| Family Tree (`family-tree`) | Mti wa Familia | Word families (-at, -an, -ig, -op) | 3 | 6–9 | 3 | The tree has a word ending such as -at. Drop a first-letter seed on it: a real word grows a fruit, a silly word grows a leaf. Level 3: make three new words from one family. |
| Duka la Herufi (`duka-la-herufi`) | Duka la Herufi | sh, ch, th | 3 | 6–9 | 3 | The shopkeeper asks for an item. Choose sh, ch or th to finish its name on the price tag, then read it. Level 2: at the end of the word. Level 3: read the whole word and find it. |
| Tricky Treasure (`tricky-treasure`) | Hazina ya Maneno | Tricky words | 3 | 6–9 | 3 | Dig in the sand at the coast. Somo says a tricky word (the, said, was); tap the shell with that word among look-alikes. It goes into your treasure book. |
| Story Strip (`story-strip`) | Mstari wa Hadithi | Story order and retelling | 2, 3 | 5–9 | 3 | Hear a short Kenyan story, put the picture cards in order (first, next, last), then answer who, where or why. Level 3: read the story yourself. |
| Safari Words (`safari-words`) | Maneno ya Safari | Word meanings (vocabulary) | 1, 2 | 5–8 | 3 | Hear what a word means ("an animal with a very long neck") and find it in the savanna or the village. Level 2: sort things into animals, food and tools. Level 3: opposites and words that mean the same. |
| Bao Sums (`bao-sums`) | Hesabu za Bao | Quick sums, Missing number in a sum (7 + ? = 10) | 2, 3 | 6–9 | 3 | Sow seeds pit by pit while Somo counts aloud, then do the sum. Level 2: start from the bigger number. Level 3: the missing number (7 + ? = 10). |
| Mizani (`mizani`) | Mizani | Equal: both sides the same (5 + 3 = ? + 2) | 3, 4 | 6–9 | 3 | At the market scale, add sacks to make both sides balance. Level 2: 5 + 3 = ? + 2. Level 3: take sacks away to balance. |
| Kiondo Patterns (`kiondo-patterns`) | Mifumo ya Kiondo | Number patterns | 1, 2 | 5–8 | 3 | Finish the bead pattern on the kiondo strap: AB, ABB, ABC. Level 3: growing number patterns like 2, 4, 6. |

Every plug-in game: 8 to 12 items a level, 3 levels, no timers, no speed rewards, never "wrong" or a red X, a hint ladder (1st miss: a nudge; 2nd miss: a worked example, then try again), every line spoken with subtitles and in Kiswahili, reading games use only letters the child has learned (Somo sends them), and every item is reported to Somo for mastery, the attempt log and telemetry. Coins come only from Somo.

## Mistake tags added for these skills

- `firstLast`: Mixed up the first and the last sound
- `syllableCount`: Counted the beats in a word wrongly
- `segCount`: Too many or too few sounds in a word
- `digraph`: Mixed up sh, ch and th
- `addedBoth`: Added both sides instead of balancing
- `nonWordReal`: Called a made-up word real (or a real word made-up)
- `sequence`: Put story events out of order
